explanations: luna: The verse forbids mixing truth with falsehood and concealing the truth while knowing it. This is a specific boundary against the source section’s movement from hidden teaching to clear public speech. | terra: The command not to conceal truth knowingly names concealment as an active covering of what should be made clear.
terra: People recite the Book yet تَنسَوْنَ أَنفُسَكُمْ; recitation without retained self-application exposes the gap between a book on the tongue and remembrance in the person.
terra: Israel is commanded to hold the revealed gift firmly and remember what is in it, the exact positive reversal of throwing scripture behind the back.

luna: A group hear God’s words and then deliberately distort them after understanding. This is a specific reversal of the source section’s preserved and clarified word: hearing and carrying revelation can also be followed by deliberate alteration.
terra: In the People-of-the-Book passage, God knows both what they conceal and what they make public, directly framing their treatment of revelation as hidden versus disclosed.
terra: The command to hold the covenant firmly and listen is answered with “we hear and disobey,” exposing the refusal that precedes casting the Book away.
terra: Gabriel brought the revelation عَلَىٰ قَلْبِكَ by God's permission, a direct Quranic counterpart to carrying the Quran inwardly in the heart.
terra: The question whether every covenant is made only for a party to cast it away begins the discard scene that 2:101 specifies as putting the Book behind their backs.

luna: A group given Scripture discards God’s Book “وَرَاءَ ظُهُورِهِمْ”; this is the source section’s ظ ه ر image of putting away and forgetting the very book that should be kept in mind. | terra: A group given scripture casts God's Book وَرَاءَ ظُهُورِهِمْ as though they did not know, the clearest repeated scene of making revealed remembrance into something left behind.
terra: Preventing God's name from being mentioned in His places of worship is the direct negative counterpart to houses raised for His name in 24:36.

luna: The verse describes those given the Book reciting it with its due recitation. This is a specific practice of carrying scripture in speech, as in the source section’s dictionary image of Qur’an borne on the tongue. | terra: Those who recite the Book with its true recitation embody the opposite of treating it as a load carried without faithful retention.

luna: “فَٱذْكُرُونِىٓ أَذْكُرْكُمْ” makes remembrance reciprocal. It directly enacts the source section’s ذ ك ر sense of remembering, while adding that the remembrance of God and people answers one another. | terra: فَٱذْكُرُونِىٓ أَذْكُرْكُمْ states the reciprocity of remembrance that the section sets against putting someone or something behind one's back.

luna: This verse condemns concealing revealed proofs and guidance after they were made clear to people in Scripture. It directly meets the source section’s movement from what is hidden to what is explained and disclosed. | terra: Those who conceal the clear proofs and guidance after God has made them clear in the Book enact the precise failure opposed by the section's opening-and-explaining movement.
terra: After 2:159 condemns concealment, this verse makes reform include وَبَيَّنُوا; its own contribution is the required reversal into active clarification.

luna: The verse condemns those who conceal what God sent down of the Book. It makes concealment a concrete refusal of the source section’s written dhikr becoming available to people. | terra: Those who conceal what God sent down of the Book turn revealed guidance back into hidden material for a petty price.

terra: Entering houses مِن ظُهُورِهَا is rejected in favor of entering through their doors, a concrete back-to-proper-entrance movement that echoes the section's passage from behind to what is brought forward.
terra: In the witnessing rule, if one woman errs the other تُذَكِّرَ her, using remembrance as the act that restores something liable to be lost.
terra: Whether people hide or disclose what is in their breasts, God knows it; inward content and outward manifestation meet at the chest.
terra: Zechariah is commanded to remember his Lord much and glorify Him morning and evening, coupling prophetic speech with sustained remembrance.
luna: The verses recited to the Prophet are called wise remembrance. This is a concrete instance of recited revelation as dhikr, corresponding to the source section’s book and spoken-word senses.

luna: The verse challenges Scripture holders who conceal truth while knowing it. It is a concrete reversal of the source section’s explanation-and-disclosure movement, though it does not use the back image. | terra: The People of the Book are asked why they conceal truth knowingly, a direct failure to make entrusted revelation manifest.

luna: Some twist their tongues with the Book so listeners think their speech belongs to Scripture, though it does not. This is a concrete misuse of the source section’s tongue-carried Book image, false public transmission rather than faithful recitation. | terra: A group twists its tongues with scripture so listeners think their speech belongs to the Book; the tongue carries revelation falsely rather than preserving and explaining it.
luna: The verse says people of God should teach the Book and study it. This is a specific practice of keeping and transmitting scripture, though it does not use the source section’s word dhikr.
terra: The discourse is a clarification for humankind and guidance and admonition for the mindful, bringing bayān together with a reminder-like warning function.

luna: The verse first requires Scripture holders to explain the revelation to people and not conceal it, then says they threw it “فَنَبَذُوهُ وَرَاءَ ظُهُورِهِمْ.” This is the source section’s root ظ ه ر in its dictionary sense of putting something behind one’s back and forgetting it, set against public explanation. | terra: Those charged to explain the scripture and not conceal it instead cast it وَرَاءَ ظُهُورِهِمْ; this directly joins explanation, concealment, and the section's back-as-forgetting image.
terra: On Judgment Day the rejecters cannot conceal any statement from God, marking the limit at which hidden speech must give way to disclosure.
terra: Some distort words and twist their tongues in religion, another corrupted form of carrying the sacred word orally.

luna: The verse says a covenant-breaking group forgot a portion of what they had been reminded of (“نَسُوا۟ حَظًّا مِّمَّا ذُكِّرُوا۟ بِهِ”). It gives the source section’s remembered/forgotten contrast a concrete scriptural setting. | terra: Covenant-breakers distort words and نَسُوا۟ حَظًّا مِّمَّا ذُكِّرُوا۟ بِهِۦ, forgetting a portion of what they were reminded, as though setting revelation behind them.

luna: About another group, the verse likewise says they forgot a portion of what they were reminded of. This is a separate instance of the source section’s central movement from reminder to loss from memory. | terra: A second covenant community likewise forgets part of what it was reminded, showing the same movement from entrusted word to neglected memory.

luna: The Messenger brings light and a clear Book, making clear much of what Scripture holders had concealed. This directly develops the source section’s passage from hidden teaching to explanation and public disclosure. | terra: The Messenger makes clear much that the People of the Book had been hiding, directly moving scripture from concealment to public explanation.
terra: After an interval between messengers, the Messenger comes making matters clear so the People of the Book cannot claim that no bearer of news reached them.

luna: The verse says those entrusted with the Torah were to guard God’s Book (“ٱسْتُحْفِظُوا۟ مِن كِتَٰبِ ٱللَّهِ”). This is a concrete human counterpart to the source section’s dictionary sense of شرح as guarding/preserving and ذ ك ر as a prophetic book.

luna: The Prophet is commanded to convey what was sent down to him. This is a concrete public-spreading counterpart to the source section’s dictionary branch of ر ف ع as disseminating and making something manifest. | terra: The Messenger must convey all that was sent down, while God protects him from people; public delivery and divine guarding meet in one commission.
terra: The Messenger's duty is delivery while God knows what people disclose and conceal, placing public proclamation beside divine knowledge of both directions.

luna: The verse says God knows people’s secret and public dealings. This is a plausible but broad parallel to the source section’s hidden/manifest axis; it describes divine knowledge, not disclosure of scripture.
terra: What the deniers used to conceal becomes apparent to them, a reversal from hidden conduct to manifest recognition.
terra: The lost carry their burdens عَلَىٰ ظُهُورِهِمْ; a back crushed by burdens is the concrete opposite of the surah's back relieved so remembrance can be raised.
terra: فَلَمَّا نَسُوا۟ مَا ذُكِّرُوا۟ بِهِۦ directly joins forgetting with the reminder previously given; the ensuing opening of worldly gates makes the neglect temporarily look like ease.
terra: If Satan makes the hearer forget an instruction, remembrance requires leaving the wrongdoing company once recollection returns.

luna: In this rebuke about Moses’ Book, people make it into separate sheets, show some, and conceal much. The scene directly stages the source section’s paired movement between a book being exposed and kept hidden. | terra: People turn revealed scripture into parchments تُبْدُونَهَا وَتُخْفُونَ كَثِيرًا, showing the same book selectively exposed and concealed rather than fully explained.

luna: The signs are explained in varied ways so that the message may be made clear to people who know. This parallels the source section’s movement from what is closed to what is explained, though the ayah does not use the root ش ر ح.
terra: The Book sent down is described as fully detailed, supporting the section's picture of scripture as an explanation rather than a concealed object.
terra: The command to leave both ظَٰهِرَ ٱلْإِثْمِ وَبَاطِنَهُ applies the manifest/hidden distinction to sin.
terra: يَشْرَحْ صَدْرَهُۥ لِلْإِسْلَٰمِ repeats the opening of a breast as the act by which God makes a person fit for guidance.
terra: The Book sent to the Prophet must cause no constriction in his breast; he is to warn through it, and it is a reminder for believers, joining chest, scripture, and remembrance.
terra: The forbidden indecencies include مَا ظَهَرَ مِنْهَا وَمَا بَطَنَ, again marking the boundary between what appears and what remains concealed.
terra: Those who forgot the meeting of their day are “forgotten” that day, a judgment reversal of reciprocal remembrance.
terra: God has brought a Book detailed with knowledge as guidance and mercy, another scriptural instance of revelation opened into explanation.

terra: Those who follow the unlettered Messenger find him written in earlier scripture, and he removes their burdens and shackles; preserved prophetic mention and relieved weight meet in the same portrait.
terra: When the transgressors forget what they had been reminded of, God rescues those who forbade evil; retained reminder here becomes a dividing line.
terra: Under the raised mountain, the community is told to hold the Book firmly and remember its contents, setting retention against later scriptural forgetting.

luna: When Qur’an is recited, listeners are told to hear it and attend in silence. The ayah supplies the hearer’s side of the source section’s spoken dhikr, making public utterance something received and retained.
terra: The command is to remember the Lord inwardly, humbly, and below the level of loud speech; remembrance can be held within rather than circulated aloud on the tongue.
terra: Believers are told not to turn their backs while hearing God and the Messenger, directly reversing the posture of audible revelation placed behind oneself.
terra: God sends the Messenger with guidance and truth لِيُظْهِرَهُۥ عَلَى ٱلدِّينِ كُلِّهِۦ; the causative of ظهر moves the message into public prevalence, beyond mere visibility.
terra: نَسُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ فَنَسِيَهُمْ gives another reciprocal forgetting scene, the negative counterpart to mutual remembrance.
terra: The Quran confirms prior revelation and provides a detailed exposition of the Book, linking faithful preservation with clarification.
terra: No deed escapes God even by an atom's weight, and all is in a clear Book; unnoticed action is preserved for manifestation.
terra: The Book's verses are made firm and then set out in detail by One wise and aware, a movement from protected formulation into exposition.
terra: People fold their breasts to hide from God, yet He knows what they conceal and disclose and what breasts contain; hidden interior and outward manifestation are joined at the chest.

luna: Shuʿayb rebukes his people for putting God behind their backs and disregarding Him (“وَرَاءَكُمْ ظِهْرِيًّا”). This gives the source section’s ظ ه ر dictionary extension a lived case: they treat God's command as forgettable. | terra: Shuayb says his people have made God وَرَاءَكُمْ ظِهْرِيًّا; the source section explicitly uses this wording for treating what should remain present as forgotten or neglected.
terra: Joseph asks a companion ٱذْكُرْنِى عِندَ رَبِّكَ, but Satan makes him forget that mention; a name meant to travel on a tongue is instead withheld by forgetting.
terra: Joseph's former companion remembers him after a long interval, completing the delayed name-on-the-tongue scene begun in 12:42.
terra: The narrative revelation confirms earlier scripture and gives a detailed exposition of all things, closely matching the source definition of zikir as a book containing religious detail.

luna: The verse places secret speech beside speech uttered openly, and what is hidden by night beside what moves about by day. It concretely echoes the source section’s hidden/manifest axis across both word and presence. | terra: Secret speech and public speech, hiding by night and moving openly by day, are all alike to God; the verse expands the hidden-manifest polarity across word and movement.
terra: Believing hearts find rest through God's remembrance, locating zikir within the heart as something retained and sustaining.
terra: Every messenger is sent in his people's language لِيُبَيِّنَ لَهُمْ, making clear speech the public function of revelation.

luna: Abraham says God knows what they conceal and declare. This is a specific but indirect parallel to the source section’s hidden/open axis; it concerns human speech before God, not scripture’s disclosure. | terra: Abraham addresses the One who knows what people conceal and disclose, placing hidden and open need before God in prayer.
terra: Opponents address the Prophet as the one to whom the Reminder was sent while accusing him of madness; even hostile speech identifies his public association with zikir.

luna: Here al-dhikr is sent down and God is its ḥāfiẓ. This joins the source section’s dictionary senses of ذ ك ر as scripture and keeping something in memory to an explicit promise of preservation. | terra: God names the revelation ٱلذِّكْرَ and undertakes its preservation, directly realizing the section's linked senses of remembrance, scripture, and guarding.
luna: God knows what people conceal and make manifest. This is a specific but indirect parallel to the source section’s hidden/manifest relation, applied to divine knowledge of human acts.
terra: Those who do not know are directed to أَهْلَ ٱلذِّكْرِ, the people who possess earlier revealed knowledge.

luna: The verse calls the revelation al-dhikr and gives the Prophet the task “لِتُبَيِّنَ لِلنَّاسِ.” It brings together the source section’s ذ ك ر as prophetic scripture and ش ر ح as making something clear to people. | terra: The Reminder is sent to the Prophet لِتُبَيِّنَ لِلنَّاسِ what was revealed, joining zikir-as-book to the section's sense of şerh as public explanation.

luna: The stated purpose of sending the Book is that the Prophet clarify what people differ about. This directly parallels the source section’s ش ر ح dictionary sense of opening what is closed, now applied to revealed teaching. | terra: The Book is sent to the Prophet only لِتُبَيِّنَ لَهُمُ what they dispute, repeating the explanatory commission of 16:44.

luna: The verse calls the sent-down Book a clarification for all things and guidance. This directly parallels the source section’s dictionary sense of ش ر ح as making something clear, now stated as the Book’s purpose. | terra: The Book sent to the Prophet is described as a clarification of everything, guidance, mercy, and good news, directly joining scripture with explanatory disclosure.
terra: The opponents allege a human teacher, but the revelation is identified as a clear Arabic tongue, stressing the public linguistic vehicle by which it is borne.
terra: مَن شَرَحَ بِٱلْكُفْرِ صَدْرًا uses the same breast-opening form for willing unbelief, a precise moral reversal of the opened breast in 94:1 and 6:125.
terra: Every person's record is fastened to the neck and brought out on Resurrection as an open book, making what was carried and hidden into a visible record.
terra: ٱقْرَأْ كِتَٰبَكَ commands the person to read that opened record, so the book itself makes forgotten deeds present to consciousness.
terra: The Quran is repeatedly varied لِيَذَّكَّرُوا۟, yet the hearers increase in aversion; abundant reminder does not guarantee retained remembrance.

luna: When Qur’an is recited, a hidden barrier is placed between the Prophet and those who deny the Hereafter (“حِجَابًا مَّسْتُورًا”). The recitation becomes concealed from its intended listeners, reversing the source section’s movement from hidden to manifest.

luna: The next ayah describes coverings over hearts and deafness in ears when the Lord alone is mentioned. It completes 17:45’s barrier by showing why the spoken reminder does not reach or move its hearers. | terra: When the Prophet mentions his Lord alone in the Quran, opponents turn عَلَىٰٓ أَدْبَٰرِهِمْ in aversion, bodily putting the spoken reminder behind them.
terra: The Prophet is promised a praised station, an indirect form of divinely elevated honor that complements the raising of his public mention.
terra: God could remove the revelation from the Prophet and leave no guardian for it; this stated possibility marks the boundary around the preservation promised in 15:9.

luna: The Qur’an is divided for people to recite it over time, with measured recitation. This directly parallels the source section’s image of scripture carried by the reader’s tongue and made public in speech. | terra: The Quran is divided so the Prophet may recite it to people over time, showing a stored revelation made public through repeated speech.
terra: وَٱذْكُر رَّبَّكَ إِذَا نَسِيتَ places remembering directly after forgetting, stating the lexical opposition developed in the section.

luna: The Prophet is told to recite what has been revealed from his Lord’s Book, whose words cannot be altered. This joins the source section’s Qur’an-on-the-tongue image to the preservation of the recited text. | terra: The Prophet is told to recite the revealed Book, whose words no one can change; oral delivery and textual preservation meet here.
terra: The record is set down and omits nothing small or great; what people may have forgotten remains preserved and visibly present.
terra: One reminded of God's signs turns away and وَنَسِىَ مَا قَدَّمَتْ يَدَاهُ, joining offered reminder, physical aversion, and forgetting.
terra: The servant reports forgetting the fish and being made to forget أَنْ أَذْكُرَهُ, again putting mention and forgetting in the same small scene.
terra: The command to mention Mary in the Book makes scripture itself the vehicle that keeps a person's story and name publicly remembered.
terra: The repeated command to mention Abraham in the Book gives his truthful prophetic name an enduring textual presence.
terra: God grants the patriarchs لِسَانَ صِدْقٍ عَلِيًّا, a high truthful mention, bringing tongue, enduring reputation, and elevation into one phrase.
terra: Moses is likewise to be mentioned in the Book, showing scripture preserving a messenger's name and character.
terra: Ishmael's mention in the Book continues the repeated pattern of prophetic names carried by revelation.
terra: Idris is to be mentioned in the Book before his raised station is stated, joining scriptural remembrance to elevation across the two verses.
terra: God raises Idris مَكَانًا عَلِيًّا; this is a different, personal use of elevation that helps distinguish raised station from raised public mention.
terra: وَمَا كَانَ رَبُّكَ نَسِيًّا assures the Prophet that his Lord is never forgetful, a boundary around the fear of neglected need or delayed revelation.

luna: The Qur’an is made easy in the Prophet’s tongue for warning and good news. This directly stages the source section’s tongue-carried revelation as speech that reaches others. | terra: God has made the revelation easy بِلِسَانِكَ so the Prophet may announce and warn; the Book is carried and made public on his tongue.
terra: The Quran was not sent down to the Prophet so that he should suffer, setting revelation against oppressive weight before the next verse calls it a reminder.

luna: The Qur’an is described as a reminder for those who fear. This is a direct instance of the source section’s dictionary sense of prophetic scripture as dhikr. | terra: The Quran of 20:2 is sent as a reminder for one who fears, giving the non-burdensome revelation its memory-making function.
terra: Whether speech is voiced aloud or withheld, God knows the secret and what is still more hidden, applying the open-hidden movement specifically to words.
terra: Moses prays رَبِّ ٱشْرَحْ لِى صَدْرِى, the exact breast-opening image voiced by another messenger before his public task.
terra: Moses says the knowledge is in a Book with his Lord and that his Lord neither errs nor forgets, uniting written record with unfailing divine memory.

luna: After recounting earlier events, the verse says God has given the Prophet a reminder from Himself. This is a specific case of revealed narrative serving as dhikr, as in the source section’s book-and-memory sense. | terra: God tells the Prophet that He narrates earlier reports and has given him مِن لَّدُنَّا ذِكْرًا, identifying the delivered book itself as remembrance.
terra: Whoever turns away from that Reminder will carry وِزْرًا on Resurrection; discarded zikir becoming a carried burden sharply reverses the surah's lifted burden and raised zikir.
terra: The Prophet is told not to hurry the Quran before its revelation is completed and to ask for increased knowledge, another boundary around faithful oral retention.

luna: Adam is said to have forgotten the covenant previously made with him (“فَنَسِىَ”). This gives the source section’s forgetting branch a specific instance where a prior divine word fails to remain held in mind.

luna: The verse’s condition is turning away from “ذِكْرِى.” It contrasts the source section’s raised remembrance with deliberate refusal of remembrance, and names the consequence that follows in its context.
terra: The reply says God's signs came but the person forgot them, so today he is forgotten; remembrance rejected becomes reciprocal forgetting.

luna: Whenever a new reminder comes to the people, they listen playfully. It shows the source section’s remembrance reaching the ear without being seriously retained. | terra: Whenever a renewed reminder comes from their Lord, people listen while playing, so delivered revelation reaches the ear without being kept.
terra: The repeated instruction to ask أَهْلَ ٱلذِّكْرِ again uses zikir for the body of remembered scriptural knowledge held by a community.

luna: The sent-down Book is described as containing the people’s dhikr (“كِتَابًا فِيهِ ذِكْرُكُمْ”). This directly meets the source section’s dictionary sense that prophetic scripture itself is dhikr. | terra: God has sent down كِتَٰبًا فِيهِ ذِكْرُكُمْ; the Book contains the hearers' reminder or mention, joining scripture with the name kept present.

luna: The verse calls the reminder for the Prophet’s generation and for those before them. It directly supports the source section’s dictionary claim that the books of earlier prophets are dhikr as well. | terra: هَٰذَا ذِكْرُ مَن مَّعِىَ وَذِكْرُ مَن قَبْلِى identifies the present and earlier prophetic scriptures as zikir, matching the source section's dictionary claim about prophets' books.

luna: Moses and Aaron are given the Criterion, light, and a dhikr for the God-fearing. It supplies a second prophetic-book instance for the source section’s dictionary claim that every prophetic book is dhikr. | terra: The scripture given to Moses and Aaron is called criterion, illumination, and ذِكْرًا, supporting the section's claim that earlier prophetic books are remembrances.

luna: The verse explicitly calls the sent-down revelation “ذِكْرٌ مُّبَارَكٌ.” It directly supports the source section’s dictionary sense of ذ ك ر as a prophetic book, here blessed and sent down. | terra: وَهَٰذَا ذِكْرٌ مُّبَارَكٌ أَنزَلْنَٰهُ calls the present revelation a blessed Reminder that has been sent down.
terra: God says He wrote in the Psalms after ٱلذِّكْرِ, where zikir denotes an antecedent divine record or scripture rather than merely an act of remembering.
terra: God knows speech spoken aloud and what people conceal, applying the open/hidden distinction specifically to utterance.
terra: Protected houses of worship are places in which God's name is mentioned abundantly, showing public remembrance preserved in built space.
terra: God brought them ذِكْرِهِمْ yet they turn away from their own reminder or honor, a pointed reversal of having one's mention raised and retained.
terra: God permits houses أَن تُرْفَعَ وَيُذْكَرَ فِيهَا ٱسْمُهُ; raising and a name circulating in speech meet exactly as they do in the section's reading of raised remembrance.
terra: The objects of worship say the people forgot the Reminder and became ruined, another explicit instance of revelation lost from active memory.
terra: A false companion leads a person away from the Reminder after it has reached him, another direct transition from present revelation to abandoned remembrance.

luna: The Prophet complains that his people took this Qur’an as “مَهْجُورًا,” abandoned. This is a specific communal counterpart to the source section’s contrast between what is cast behind the back and what is retained and raised as dhikr. | terra: The Messenger complains that his people took this Quran مَهْجُورًا; abandonment is the nonlexical equivalent of putting the Book behind one's back.
terra: The Quran is delivered gradually لِنُثَبِّتَ بِهِۦ فُؤَادَكَ and recited distinctly, linking ordered recitation with the Prophet's inward firmness.
terra: Each challenge is answered with truth and أَحْسَنَ تَفْسِيرًا; the verse contributes the revelation's explanatory response to what is brought forward.
terra: The warning has been distributed among people لِيَذَّكَّرُوا۟, but most refuse except in ingratitude, contrasting dissemination with reception.
terra: No renewed reminder comes from the Merciful without their turning away, a recurring scripture-behind-the-back movement.
terra: Abraham asks for لِسَانَ صِدْقٍ فِى ٱلْءَاخِرِينَ, a truthful mention on later tongues; it is a direct nonlexical parallel to an honored name made to endure publicly.

luna: The passage says the faithful spirit brought the revelation; 26:194 locates it on the Prophet’s heart and 26:195 calls it a clear Arabic tongue. This begins a concrete hidden-to-spoken route parallel to the source section’s heart-memory and tongue-carried Qur’an.

luna: This ayah locates the revelation on the Prophet’s heart so he can warn, completing 26:193’s arrival and anticipating the clear Arabic tongue of 26:195. It closely parallels the source section’s memorization in the heart before speech. | terra: The trustworthy Spirit brings the revelation عَلَىٰ قَلْبِكَ so the Prophet may warn, linking inward reception to outward speech.

luna: The next ayah names a clear Arabic tongue (“بِلِسَانٍ عَرَبِيٍّ مُّبِينٍ”). It completes 26:193–194’s movement from revelation to heart to speech, like the source section’s Qur’an borne on the tongue. | terra: بِلِسَانٍ عَرَبِىٍّ مُّبِينٍ completes the heart-reception scene with a clear Arabic tongue, moving the revelation from inwardly held to manifest speech.
terra: God brings forth what is hidden in the heavens and earth and knows what people conceal and disclose, explicitly staging the emergence of the hidden.
terra: Nothing hidden in heaven or earth lies outside a clear Book, joining concealment with comprehensive written preservation.

luna: This Qur’an relates to the Children of Israel much of what they differ about. That gives a specific interpretive parallel to the source section’s dictionary sense of ش ر ح as explanation, although this ayah says it recounts rather than using the source term.

luna: The verse says the Word has been conveyed to the people so that they may remember. It directly meets the source section’s account of a word spread outward and dhikr as what brings something back to mind.

terra: Before the clear signs of 29:49 are held in learned breasts, the Prophet had neither recited a prior book nor written one by hand; the verse distinguishes inwardly received Quran from ordinary textual acquisition.
terra: The revelation is ءَايَٰتٌۢ بَيِّنَٰتٌ فِى صُدُورِ those given knowledge: clear signs preserved within breasts are the Quran held without an external book.

luna: The verse asks whether it is not enough that the Book was sent down and is recited to them, and calls it mercy and reminder for believers. It concretely joins the source section’s Book-as-dhikr to public recitation.
terra: ظَهَرَ ٱلْفَسَادُ describes corruption becoming manifest on land and sea; it uses the section's emergence sense of ظهر for an adverse thing made visible.
terra: When God's signs are recited, the arrogant person turns away as though he had not heard, bodily enacting the refusal to retain spoken revelation.
terra: God's favors are bestowed ظَٰهِرَةً وَبَاطِنَةً, using the same outer/hidden polarity for gifts rather than for words.
terra: “Today We forget you as you forgot the meeting of this day” turns chosen forgetfulness into experienced abandonment.

luna: When reminded of God’s signs, believers fall prostrate and glorify Him rather than act arrogantly. This supplies a concrete receptive response to reminder, in contrast to the source section’s images of putting a word aside.
terra: The person reminded of the Lord's signs then turns away enacts the same sequence as receiving and discarding scripture.
terra: The Prophet's household is told to remember what is recited in their homes of God's signs and wisdom, joining oral recitation with deliberate retention.
terra: Men and women who remember God abundantly are named together, another exact Quranic realization of abundant remembrance.
terra: The messengers convey God's messages and fear no one but Him, stating public delivery as the stance required of those entrusted with revelation.
terra: Believers are commanded to remember God with abundant remembrance, directly exemplifying the section's dictionary gloss of zikrā as much remembering.
terra: God and the angels bless the Prophet and believers are commanded to bless and greet him, a concrete practice by which his mention continually circulates.
terra: Nothing even of minute weight is hidden from God without being in a clear Book, making the record the place where the unseen remains present.

luna: The Prophet is to warn by the Qur’an those who follow the reminder and fear the unseen. This makes the source section’s dhikr a recited warning that a hearer follows, rather than merely a word retained privately.
terra: God writes what people send ahead and the traces they leave, enumerating everything in a clear register; what passes is preserved and made legible.

luna: The Prophet is not taught poetry; the revelation is a reminder and a clear Qur’an. This specifies the source section’s spoken dhikr as clear revealed speech, and distinguishes it from another kind of utterance. | terra: The Prophet was not taught poetry; the revelation is إِلَّا ذِكْرٌ وَقُرْءَانٌ مُّبِينٌ, explicitly joining Reminder, Quran, and manifest clarity.
terra: God knows both what hostile speakers conceal and what they declare, so unvoiced and voiced words are equally present to Him.
terra: God leaves Noah's truthful mention among later generations, a direct example of a prophet's name being preserved after him.
terra: The same formula leaves Abraham's mention among later peoples, realizing the enduring tongue-of-truth he requested in 26:84.
terra: Moses and Aaron likewise receive a mention left among later generations, extending the pattern of divinely sustained prophetic memory.
terra: Elijah's mention is also left among later generations, another instance of a prophetic name made to remain in communal speech.
terra: The opponents ask whether the Reminder was sent specifically to this Prophet from among them, exposing their resentment at the distinction conferred by revelation.

luna: The Book is sent down as blessed so people may reflect on its verses and those of understanding take reminder. This directly joins written revelation to the source section’s dictionary senses of book-as-dhikr and recalling through it.
terra: The person whose breast God has opened to submission is set against hearts hardened مِن ذِكْرِ ٱللَّهِ, bringing شرح الصدر and remembrance into one verse.

luna: The sent-down Book is described as repeated and mutually reinforcing, and its hearers’ hearts soften toward remembrance of God. The bridge to the source section’s “many remembrances” gloss is interpretive: here repetition describes the scripture and its effect. | terra: After 39:22 joins opened breast and remembrance, this verse calls revelation the best discourse, a consistent Book, and describes hearts softening to God's remembrance.

luna: The Qur’an gives every kind of example so that people may remember. This connects the source section’s dictionary sense of tadhkira, a means by which something is remembered, to a particular teaching method in revelation.
terra: When God alone is mentioned, the hearts of those denying the Hereafter recoil, while mention of others brings delight; spoken remembrance exposes inward reception.
terra: The revelation is a Book whose verses have been fully set out as an Arabic Quran for people who know, embodying scripture made clear.
terra: Although 41:3 presents an explained Book, most people turn away and do not listen; their refusal reverses the intended movement from revelation to hearing.

luna: The disbelievers urge one another not to listen to the Qur’an and to make noise during its recitation. This is a specific obstruction of the source section’s word moving aloud and being heard or remembered.

luna: Those who disbelieve in the Reminder when it comes to them are condemned, though it is a mighty Book. This concretely stages rejection of the source section’s book-as-dhikr when it becomes present to its audience. | terra: The revelation is itself ٱلذِّكْرِ and also كِتَٰبٌ عَزِيزٌ, directly supporting the section's identification of remembrance with the Book.
terra: Continuing 41:41, falsehood cannot reach the Book مِنۢ بَيْنِ يَدَيْهِ وَلَا مِنْ خَلْفِهِۦ; protection from front and behind answers the image of scripture put behind backs.
terra: The question whether God should turn ٱلذِّكْرَ away from a transgressing people reverses the usual scene: here withholding revelation is posed as a divine response.
terra: Abraham makes the declaration a word lasting among his descendants so they may return, a concrete model of speech preserved across generations.

luna: Whoever turns away from the remembrance of the Merciful is assigned a companion. This is a specific refusal of the source section’s remembered word, with a consequence attached to turning away. | terra: Whoever turns blindly away from the Merciful's remembrance is assigned a satanic companion, giving neglect of zikir a concrete consequence.

luna: The Qur’an is called a dhikr for the Prophet and his people, who will be questioned about it. This makes the source section’s book-as-dhikr a public relation between recited revelation and its audience. | terra: The revelation is ذِكْرٌ لَّكَ وَلِقَوْمِكَ, meaning reminder and plausibly honor or lasting mention; that semantic overlap directly illuminates the Prophet's raised zikir.
terra: God hears secret speech and private counsel while His messengers write it down, turning hidden words into a preserved record.

luna: The Qur’an is made easy upon the Prophet’s tongue so people may remember (“بِلِسَانِكَ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَذَكَّرُونَ”). This closely joins the source section’s tongue-carried Qur’an to its account of remembrance. | terra: فَإِنَّمَا يَسَّرْنَٰهُ بِلِسَانِكَ لَعَلَّهُمْ يَتَذَكَّرُونَ explicitly joins revelation made easy on the Prophet's tongue with the hearers' remembering.
terra: The sinner hears God's signs recited yet persists as though he had not heard them, another exact image of a word reaching the ear but being discarded.
terra: God's Book speaks against people in truth because their deeds were being copied, joining preserved record with public testimony.
terra: The same reciprocal verdict is stated again: rejection and forgetting of the meeting result in being left forgotten.
luna: A group of jinn listen to the Qur’an, then return to their people as warners. This concretely stages the source section’s word carried aloud and disseminated from one audience to another.

luna: The next ayah reports the jinn identifying what they heard as a Book sent down after Moses and guiding to truth. Its own contribution is to name the heard recitation as scripture, matching the source section’s prophetic-book sense of dhikr.
luna: The jinn then urge their people to answer God’s caller and believe. This completes the transmission begun in 46:29–30 with the response sought from those who hear the message.
terra: Those who turn back after guidance has become clear embody both movements at once: disclosure occurs, then the recipient places it behind him.
terra: The same promise that the true religion will be made manifest or prevailing repeats the public expansion side of the ظهر root.
terra: God knows what the earth diminishes of the dead, and with Him is a preserving Book; divine record safeguards what disappears from sight.
terra: The two receiving recorders sit on the right and left, establishing the agents who preserve each person's otherwise passing acts.
terra: No word is uttered without a watcher ready to record it, turning speech on the tongue into an enduring written account.
luna: The verse says there is a reminder for one who has a heart or gives ear while present. This connects the source section’s memory held in the heart with its spoken word that reaches a listener.

luna: The Prophet is told to remind by the Qur’an whoever fears God’s warning. This directly connects the source section’s book-as-dhikr to the public act of reminding through recitation. | terra: The Prophet is to remind with the Quran whoever fears the warning, making the Book the spoken instrument of recollection.

luna: The command “remind” is justified because reminder benefits believers. It concretely extends the source section’s dhikr from preserved memory to speech that renews memory in an audience. | terra: The Prophet is told to remind because remembrance benefits believers, emphasizing zikir as an outward act that preserves an inward truth.
terra: The oath by a written Book makes the remembered word a fixed inscription.
terra: فِى رَقٍّ مَّنشُورٍ adds an unrolled, spread-open parchment, bringing written preservation into manifest view.

luna: The Prophet is told to remind and not to be a soothsayer or mad. This is a specific prophetic use of the reminder-word developed in the source section, though the surrounding polemic is distinct.

luna: After the account of Noah’s people, the verse says the Qur’an has been made easy for remembrance and asks who will remember. This directly joins the source section’s remembrance and repeated reminder to a recited scripture. | terra: God has made the Quran easy لِلذِّكْرِ and asks whether anyone will take reminder, directly linking the Book with retention and recollection.

luna: After the account of ʿĀd, the same refrain says the Qur’an is made easy for remembrance and asks who will remember. The repeated occurrence shows the source section’s “many remembrances” sense enacted across distinct warnings. | terra: This repeated declaration again presents the Quran as made easy for remembrance, showing that the invitation to retain it is deliberate and recurrent.

luna: After the account of Thamud, this refrain again makes the Qur’an easy for remembrance. Its placement after another people’s fate concretely repeats the source section’s reminder/retention relation. | terra: The third repetition renews the same Quran-and-memory relation after another warning narrative.

luna: After Lot’s people, the refrain again asks who will remember the Qur’an made easy for remembrance. This is a separate contextual instance of the source section’s repeated dhikr. | terra: The fourth repetition closes the sequence by again making remembrance the intended human response to the preserved recitation.
terra: Everything people have done is preserved in written records, giving deeds a textual memory beyond human forgetting.
terra: Every small and great deed is inscribed, completing 54:52 with the record's exhaustive scope.

luna: The Merciful is said to have taught the Qur’an. This is a specific instance of the prophetic Book as taught discourse, corresponding to the source section’s dictionary sense of dhikr as scripture. | terra: The Merciful teaches the Quran, establishing the revealed object whose human articulation and explanation the following verses describe.

luna: The verse says the Merciful taught al-bayān. The source section explicitly gives al-bayān as the dictionary wording for ش ر ح; this ayah names that clarifying expression as something taught. | terra: God teaches the human being clear expression, completing 55:2's Quran-teaching scene with the capacity for articulate explanation.
terra: إِنَّهُۥ لَقُرْءَانٌ كَرِيمٌ identifies the noble recitation before the next verse locates it within a concealed book.
terra: فِى كِتَٰبٍ مَّكْنُونٍ places the recited Quran in a hidden or protected Book, a boundary between concealed source and voiced revelation.
terra: God is ٱلظَّٰهِرُ وَٱلْبَاطِنُ, the Quran's most compressed pairing of the manifest and the hidden.
terra: The wall's بَاطِنُهُ contains mercy while its ظَاهِرُهُ faces punishment, giving the hidden/manifest pair sharply opposite contents.

luna: Believers are asked whether the time has come for their hearts to humble themselves at God’s remembrance and the truth sent down. This links the source section’s remembrance to the inward retention and response of its hearers.
terra: God has enumerated the deeds that people forgot, showing divine preservation bringing forgotten acts back into view on the Day of Resurrection.
terra: God raises believers and those given knowledge in degrees, another honor-bestowing sense of رفع alongside the section's sense of making mention public.

luna: Satan makes a people forget the remembrance of God (“أَنسَىٰهُمْ ذِكْرَ ٱللَّهِ”). This is a direct counter-image to the source section’s preserved and raised dhikr: remembrance is displaced rather than retained. | terra: Satan makes a people forget ذِكْرَ ٱللَّهِ, explicitly placing induced forgetting against remembrance.

luna: The warning not to forget God, followed by God making them forget themselves, develops the source section’s memory/forgetting axis as a loss that alters self-knowledge, not merely a missed word. | terra: Those who forgot God were made to forget themselves, a reciprocal reversal that darkens the promise أَذْكُرْكُمْ in 2:152.
terra: Had the Quran descended upon a mountain, it would have become humbled and split from fear of God; this gives revealed speech a figurative weight capable of crushing what bears it.
terra: A third occurrence again links the Messenger's mission with making the true religion manifest over all religion.
terra: Those entrusted with the Torah but failing to bear it are likened to a donkey carrying books, a sharp counterimage to scripture truly carried in memory and speech.

luna: Believers are warned not to let wealth or children distract them from God’s remembrance. This is a specific rival to the source section’s keeping dhikr in mind: worldly attention can displace it.
terra: God knows what people conceal and declare and knows what breasts contain, another direct passage from inward storage to outward speech.

luna: Whether people conceal their speech or say it aloud, God knows what is within the breasts. This is a close parallel to the source section’s passage from hidden to spoken, while locating knowledge of both with God. | terra: Whether speech is kept secret or voiced openly, God knows what is within breasts; tongue, hiddenness, and inward keeping are held together.
luna: The Qur’an is described as a reminder to all worlds. This supports the source section’s specific dictionary sense of prophetic scripture itself as dhikr, with a universal audience.

luna: The event is made a reminder, “وَتَعِيَهَآ أُذُنٌ وَٰعِيَةٌ,” so an attentive ear retains it. This gives bodily form to the source section’s dictionary definition of dhikr as keeping something in memory. | terra: The ark-event is made تَذْكِرَةً and retained by أُذُنٌ وَٰعِيَةٌ; a reminder-object and the organ that preserves it are explicitly paired.
terra: The person handed the record in the right hand publicly invites others to read it, turning a private record into glad, open proclamation.
terra: The right-hand recipient says he knew he would meet his reckoning, contributing retained awareness to the openly displayed book scene of 69:19.
terra: The person given the record in the left hand wishes it had never been received, another judgment reversal of scripture as honored reminder.
terra: The left-hand recipient wishes he had not known his record, turning the manifest book into knowledge he longs to escape.
terra: The Quran is called تَذْكِرَةٌ لِّلْمُتَّقِينَ, directly exemplifying a reminder as the thing by which truth is recalled.

luna: A group of jinn hear the recitation and repeat that they have heard a wondrous Qur’an. This directly stages the source section’s spoken word becoming something an audience remembers and reports.

luna: The next ayah says that the Qur’an guides to the right way and that the listeners believe in it. It gives the response to the hearing scene in 72:1, showing the public recitation retained as guidance.

luna: The verse says God knows the unseen and “فَلَا يُظْهِرُ عَلَىٰ غَيْبِهِۦٓ أَحَدًا.” The source section’s root ظ ه ر includes a hidden thing becoming manifest; this ayah sets a boundary on who can disclose the unseen. | terra: God is عَٰلِمُ ٱلْغَيْبِ and does not يُظْهِرُ anyone upon His unseen; the same root that can mean becoming manifest here marks divine control over disclosure.

luna: Following 72:26, this ayah specifies the exception: a messenger whom God approves, with guards before and behind him. Its own contribution is to make the source section’s disclosure boundary selective rather than absolute. | terra: The exception to 72:26 allows disclosure of the unseen to a chosen messenger and stations guards around him; hidden knowledge becomes guarded revelation.

luna: The next ayah explains that the messengers must convey their Lord’s messages and that God encompasses what they have. It completes 72:27’s guarded exception with the public conveyance that the source section associates with making the hidden manifest. | terra: The guarded disclosure serves that messengers have delivered their Lord's messages, completing the sequence from hidden knowledge to protected public communication.

luna: The Prophet is told to recite the Qur’an in measured recitation. This is a specific oral practice corresponding to the source section’s dictionary image of bearing the Qur’an on the tongue. | terra: The Prophet is commanded to recite the Quran in a measured way immediately before it is called a weighty word, making disciplined tongue-bearing part of the burden image.
terra: God will cast upon the Prophet a weighty word, a precise counterpoint to the section's claim that the back can carry sacred speech rather than an ordinary load.
terra: إِنَّ هَٰذِهِۦ تَذْكِرَةٌ presents the recited warning itself as a reminder that can guide a chosen path.
terra: فَمَا لَهُمْ عَنِ ٱلتَّذْكِرَةِ مُعْرِضِينَ asks why they turn bodily and mentally away from the reminder, closely matching scripture put behind the back.
terra: كَأَنَّهُمْ حُمُرٌ مُّسْتَنفِرَةٌ gives the turners-away a visible herd image; its contribution is the panic embodied in their rejection of reminder.
terra: فَرَّتْ مِن قَسْوَرَةٍ completes the fleeing-herd comparison, showing how emphatically the reminder has been put behind them.

luna: The passage calls the Qur’an a reminder. This directly meets the source section’s dictionary sense of dhikr as scripture and a reminder, before 74:55 specifies a hearer’s response. | terra: كَلَّآ إِنَّهُۥ تَذْكِرَةٌ reasserts that the very revelation from which they flee is a reminder-object.

luna: The following ayah says whoever wills may remember it. It completes 74:54’s reminder with the act of keeping it in mind, as in the source section’s definition of dhikr. | terra: فَمَن شَآءَ ذَكَرَهُۥ answers flight with the possibility of retaining the reminder in mind.

luna: The next ayah says they will not remember unless God wills. It adds a limit to the reminder and willing response in 74:54–55, resonating with the source section’s distinction between what is recalled and what remains hidden.

luna: The Prophet is told not to move his tongue hastily with revelation, “لَا تُحَرِّكْ بِهِۦ لِسَانَكَ.” This concretely meets the source section’s dictionary image of carrying Qur’an on the tongue while preserving it. | terra: The Prophet is told not to move his tongue hurriedly with the revelation, directly staging the section's image of Quran borne on the tongue.

luna: The next ayah assigns the collection and recitation of revelation to God (“جَمْعَهُۥ وَقُرْءَانَهُۥ”). It completes 75:16’s tongue-and-retention scene with the source section’s concern for what is kept and recited. | terra: إِنَّ عَلَيْنَا جَمْعَهُۥ وَقُرْءَانَهُ makes collecting and reciting the revelation God's responsibility, a close parallel to divine preservation and protected memory.

luna: After the promise of collection in 75:17, this ayah tells the Prophet to follow the recitation when it is recited. Its own contribution is the audible transmission that corresponds to the source section’s Qur’an carried on the tongue. | terra: The command to follow the revelation's recitation continues the oral scene and distinguishes faithful reception from casting the Book aside.

luna: After collection and recitation (75:17–18), God also undertakes its bayān. The source section’s dictionary branch of ش ر ح means explaining/opening; this ayah places clarification after the received recitation. | terra: ثُمَّ إِنَّ عَلَيْنَا بَيَانَهُ makes its explanation God's undertaking, directly matching the section's dictionary sense of şerh as bayān.

luna: The verse identifies the Qur’an as a reminder and invites whoever wills to take a way to the Lord. It concretely joins remembered revelation to a hearer’s response, as in the source section’s account of dhikr. | terra: The discourse is again called تَذْكِرَةٌ, with remembering meant to lead the hearer toward the Lord.
luna: The ayah says a reminder may benefit its hearer. It directly matches the source section’s dictionary definition of tadhkira as what enables remembering.

luna: The passage calls the recited message a reminder (“تَذْكِرَةٌ”), matching the source section’s dictionary sense of a tadhkira as that by which something is remembered. | terra: كَلَّآ إِنَّهَا تَذْكِرَةٌ names the revelation a reminder-object, exactly the section's definition of tezkire as that by which something is remembered.

luna: The next ayah says whoever wills may remember it (“ذَكَرَهُۥ”). It completes 80:11’s reminder with the act of retaining it, as in the source section’s account of dhikr. | terra: فَمَن شَآءَ ذَكَرَهُۥ states the human act elicited by that reminder: whoever wills keeps it in remembrance.

luna: The reminder of 80:11–12 is in honored pages (“صُحُفٍ مُّكَرَّمَةٍ”). This gives a written form to the source section’s dictionary sense of dhikr as prophetic scripture. | terra: فِى صُحُفٍ مُّكَرَّمَةٍ locates the reminder of 80:11-12 in honored pages, making the remembered thing explicitly scriptural.

luna: The pages of 80:13 are “مَّرْفُوعَةٍ مُّطَهَّرَةٍ.” The same source-section root ر ف ع that can mean spreading or making manifest is used here for pages physically elevated; that difference sharpens the image rather than equating the senses. | terra: مَّرْفُوعَةٍ مُّطَهَّرَةٍ describes those reminder-pages as raised and purified, an exact meeting of raisedness and scripture-as-zikir.

luna: The elevated pages of 80:13–14 are in the hands of scribes. This completes the passage’s physical transmission of written reminder, alongside the source section’s parallel image of Qur’an carried on the tongue.
terra: وَإِذَا ٱلصُّحُفُ نُشِرَتْ pictures records spread open, a material version of what was hidden becoming public and readable.
terra: At the upheaval each soul learns what it sent ahead and left behind, as formerly hidden conduct becomes present knowledge.
terra: Guardians are appointed over people, beginning the explanation of how their acts remain preserved.
terra: The guardians are noble recorders, making their protective oversight specifically an act of writing.
terra: The recorders know what people do, completing the passage's account of deeds kept for disclosure.
terra: Receiving the record in the right hand provides the explicit favorable counterpart to 84:10's record handed from behind the back.

luna: The recipient is given his record “وَرَاءَ ظَهْرِهِ.” The source section’s back-as-forgetting image turns into its judgmental reversal: the book once put aside returns behind the bearer as an unavoidable record. | terra: Receiving one's record وَرَاءَ ظَهْرِهِ turns the discarded-behind-the-back image into a judgment scene: the book once put behind returns behind the person.
terra: The recipient of the book from behind the back calls for destruction; this verse supplies the immediate human consequence of the posture in 84:10.
terra: Entering the Blaze completes the adverse book-behind-back scene begun in 84:10.
terra: بَلْ هُوَ قُرْءَانٌ مَّجِيدٌ identifies what is being guarded as the glorious Quran.

luna: The Qur’an is located in a preserved tablet (“فِى لَوْحٍ مَّحْفُوظٍ”). This concretely joins the source section’s book-as-dhikr and keeping/guarding senses to a preserved written record. | terra: فِى لَوْحٍ مَّحْفُوظٍ completes 85:21 with a preserved tablet, giving a concrete scriptural form to the section's guarding sense.
terra: يَوْمَ تُبْلَى ٱلسَّرَآئِرُ names the day when inner secrets are exposed or tested, a broad eschatological realization of hidden becoming manifest.

luna: The promise “سَنُقْرِئُكَ فَلَا تَنسَىٰ” directly reverses the source section’s forgotten thing put behind one’s back: God will recite to the Prophet and he will not forget. | terra: The promise سَنُقْرِئُكَ فَلَا تَنسَىٰ gives the Prophet recitation without forgetting, matching the section's Quran carried from memory rather than from a written page.
terra: The qualification after 87:6 says God knows ٱلْجَهْرَ وَمَا يَخْفَىٰ, joining protected recitation with His knowledge of what is spoken openly and what remains hidden.

luna: The Prophet is told to remind when reminder benefits. This directly parallels the source section’s dictionary description of tadhkira as what enables remembering, now as a prophetic address. | terra: After the promise that the Prophet will recite without forgetting, he is commanded to remind wherever the reminder benefits.

luna: The next ayah says the one who fears will remember (“سَيَذَّكَّرُ مَن يَخْشَىٰ”). It completes 87:9’s reminder with the listener’s retention, matching the source section’s account of dhikr. | terra: The one who fears will take the reminder, supplying the receptive hearer for the Prophet's command to remind in 87:9.
luna: The one most wretched avoids that reminder, reversing the remembering listener of 87:10. The pair makes visible the source section’s divide between what is held in mind and what is put away.
luna: The successful person remembers the name of his Lord and prays. This is a concrete instance of the source section’s ذ ك ر as keeping a thing in mind and letting it be present in utterance.

luna: The Prophet is commanded to remind, and identified as a reminder-giver. This directly parallels the source section’s account of dhikr as something that brings a thing back to mind. | terra: فَذَكِّرْ إِنَّمَآ أَنتَ مُذَكِّرٌ gives the Prophet the role of actively bringing the reminder to mind through speech.
luna: The next ayah says the Prophet is not a controller over them. It bounds the reminder-command of 88:21: the word can be made public, but its hearers cannot be compelled to retain it.
terra: مَا وَدَّعَكَ رَبُّكَ وَمَا قَلَىٰ assures the same Prophet that his Lord has not abandoned him, the personal counterpart to a need not put behind the back.
terra: The Prophet is commanded فَحَدِّثْ of his Lord's favor, another movement from a received gift into openly circulating speech.
luna: The opening command is to read in the name of the Lord. This gives a specific recitation scene for the source section’s image of a reader bearing Qur’an on the tongue.

luna: The ayah says God taught by the pen. Alongside the reading command in 96:1, it supplies the written side of the source section’s paired images of remembered scripture and Qur’an carried in speech.
luna: A messenger recites purified pages. The verse stages the source section’s two forms of carrying revelation: an inscribed book and its movement on a reader’s tongue.

luna: The pages recited in 98:2 contain upright writings. This ayah’s contribution is to identify the content of the spoken pages, corresponding to the source section’s dictionary sense of prophetic books as dhikr.
terra: وَحُصِّلَ مَا فِى ٱلصُّدُورِ brings out what is inside breasts, reversing inward concealment into disclosure.
